title: What If a 66-Foot Rock Exploded Over a City? One Did

scenes.text: What if a rock exploded over a city? In 2013, one did. Nobody saw it coming.
It was roughly 20 meters wide and hit the atmosphere at about 42,000 miles an hour.
About 19 miles up, it blew apart with the energy of roughly 500 kilotons of TNT.
Minutes later the shockwave arrived. It damaged about 7,200 buildings across six cities.
About 1,500 people went to hospitals and clinics.
The strangest part: no telescope caught it first. It came out of the Sun's glare, hidden until it hit the air.

description:
What if a rock the size of a building exploded over a city?
In 2013 a roughly 20-meter asteroid blew apart over Chelyabinsk, Russia, releasing about 500 kilotons of energy and damaging thousands of buildings.
